content.value_statement: Playwright suites often become flaky when tests depend on brittle selectors or shared state. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for reliable end-to-end tests.
actual_capabilities: Prioritizes resilient Playwright locators by role, label, visible text, alt text, title, and test ID.
Shows Page Object Model patterns with reusable page classes and safe interaction helpers.
Recommends web-first assertions and avoids hardcoded waits that create flaky tests.
Explains fixtures, worker-scoped setup, authentication reuse, and per-test data isolation.
Covers route mocking, HAR replay, Playwright configuration, and concise test reporters.
Provides debugging commands and a suggested project structure for Playwright suites.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a runnable Playwright plugin or test generator.
Examples require adaptation to each application, authentication flow, and API shape.
It does not verify selectors against a live browser unless the agent runs Playwright separately.
Teams must still protect stored authentication state and test credentials.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Existing Tests
use_cases.description: Refactor fragile selectors, hardcoded waits, and repeated login flows into resilient Playwright patterns.

use_cases.title: Build New Test Suites
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable structure with fixtures, page objects, setup projects, and clear configuration.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI Runs
use_cases.description: Tune reporters, retries, workers, traces, screenshots, and web server settings for automated pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single Playwright test file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Playwright test for flaky selectors, missing awaits, hardcoded waits, and weak assertions. Suggest concise fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Selectors
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve locator quality in an existing test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these Playwright locators to prefer roles, labels, text, alt text, titles, and test IDs. Explain each change briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Design Fixtures
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan reusable setup for a growing test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright fixtures for this feature. Include per-test setup, worker-scoped setup, cleanup boundaries, and auth state reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of Playwright execution in CI and AI agent contexts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Playwright configuration for CI stability. Address reporters, retries, workers, traces, screenshots, web server reuse, and auth setup.

output_examples.input: A test uses CSS classes, fixed waits, and manual visibility checks.
output: Replace class selectors with role or label locators where possible.
Use web-first assertions so Playwright waits for the expected state.
Remove fixed waits and wait through user-facing page conditions.

output_examples.input: A suite logs in through the UI before every test.
output: Create a setup project that authenticates once and saves browser state.
Use stored state in dependent browser projects.
Keep the authentication file out of version control.

output_examples.input: CI output is too verbose for an AI coding agent session.
output: Use a line or dot reporter for command-line runs.
Keep traces, screenshots, and videos focused on failed or retried tests.
Avoid reporter output that consumes the agent context window.

best_practices: Prefer user-facing locators before test IDs, CSS selectors, or XPath.
Use Playwright fixtures to isolate setup, teardown, and shared worker resources.
Run CLI tests with concise reporters in CI and AI agent contexts.
anti_patterns: Do not use fixed timeouts when locators or assertions can wait for state.
Do not share mutable data across tests that must run independently.
Do not repeat UI login in every test when stored auth state is available.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents write and refactor Playwright tests using stable locators, fixtures, assertions, and CI-friendly configuration.

faq.question: Does it run Playwright tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The agent must still run commands when execution is needed.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript Playwright tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use TypeScript patterns with the Playwright test runner.

faq.question: How does it reduce flaky tests?
faq.answer: It favors web-first assertions, accessible locators, isolated data, and predictable setup through fixtures.

faq.question: Does it handle test credentials safely?
faq.answer: It recommends environment variables and stored auth state. Teams must keep auth files out of version control.
